agree.reason: The trend data, the milestones and the six-month review give cautious members a safe way to vote yes, but the two ad-background members are never told why ads must stop rather than run alongside membership during the ramp-up, and the unfilled placeholders on reserves and the ad colleague's future leave key questions open.

honest.reason: It turns the brief's "will replace within a year" into a stated goal, its figures check out (36%, 1.5%, about $20,350, 875 members), and it leaves unknowns as placeholders instead of inventing them; still, the annualized pilot revenue quietly assumes every pilot member stays, and "achievable" is asserted without support.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives the decline rate, a projection of about $67k, the members needed, the share of the list and the 4x multiple, but it misses the most favourable pace comparison (the pilot added about 35 members a week, while the target needs only about 17 a week), and it measures against gross $84k even after arguing that the shrinking net is the real benchmark.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the status quo accurately, as a declining line projected to about $67k next year with net revenue shrinking further, though the net figure is left blank.

qualification.reason: The dated milestones (400 by March 31, 600 by June 30, 875 by December 31) come with a board review and named fallback options, though "fall well short" sets no exact trigger number.

objections.reason: It covers the cash gap and the long-serving ad colleague, at least as placeholders, but it never answers the central objection from the sales-minded members, which is why ads must be dropped rather than kept during the transition, and pilot churn goes unaddressed.

fit.reason: It is a clear, sectioned memo of about one page that ends in a specific board action, though several bracketed placeholders still need filling.
